vopros: Should I pay for a tool that tracks whether ChatGPT and other AI assistants mention my business, or hire someone to get my business recommended by AI?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Yes—but I’d distinguish between “measurement” and “optimization.” If you’re a typical small or midsize business, I would usually spend a little on measurement before paying someone significant money for “AI optimization.”

AI recommendations aren't a single stable ranking. ChatGPT can use current web information, product feeds, and other sources depending on the query, and results can vary with what the customer asks. OpenAI says public websites can appear in ChatGPT Search and recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot so content can be discovered and cited. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856?utm_source=openai)) Google similarly says its existing SEO fundamentals remain relevant to its generative AI features, rather than requiring some separate secret AEO/GEO technique. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features?utm_source=openai))

So I'd approach it in this order:

- First, manually test 20–50 questions that actual prospects might ask: “best [service] in Los Angeles,” “alternatives to [competitor],” “best [product] for X,” “who should I hire for Y,” etc. Test ChatGPT, Gemini/Google AI, and whichever other assistants matter to your customers.
- Second, check whether AI is actually producing commercial recommendations in your category and whether competitors repeatedly show up while you don't.
- Third, make sure the fundamentals are good: crawlability, accurate business/product information, substantive pages explaining what you do and who it's for, reviews/reputation, third-party mentions, and traditional search visibility. For ecommerce specifically, current product data matters; OpenAI supports merchant product data and direct feeds, and Shopify catalog data is integrated into ChatGPT. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-improved-shopping-results-from-chatgpt-search%25252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525253F.mkv?utm_source=openai))
- Then consider a tracking tool if manual testing has become too cumbersome. The value is primarily monitoring changes, prompts, competitors, citations, and trends—not revealing some authoritative “ChatGPT ranking.” Google explicitly warns that third-party SEO/AEO/GEO tools don't have access to its internal ranking data and cannot guarantee performance. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/third-party-seo?authuser=50&utm_source=openai))
- Hire an expert only if they're going to improve real underlying signals—not sell you an “AI recommendation hack.” Useful work can include technical SEO, entity/business information cleanup, product feeds, content, digital PR, review/reputation strategy, and earning legitimate third-party coverage.

There are also increasingly useful free first-party measurements. For example, Bing Webmaster Tools introduced AI Performance reporting in 2026 showing citations in generative answers, while ChatGPT referrals can be identified through its `utm_source=chatgpt.com` parameter. ([blogs.bing.com](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/February-2026/Introducing-AI-Performance-in-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-Public-Preview?utm_source=openai)) That reduces the need to immediately buy an expensive dashboard.

The bigger warning sign is anyone promising something like “We can get ChatGPT to recommend you.” Nobody outside the platforms controls that outcome. Google specifically advises against things such as pursuing inauthentic mentions and other purported AEO/GEO hacks. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?authuser=4&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

If you tell me what kind of business you have (local service, SaaS, ecommerce, professional services, etc.) and roughly how much you're considering spending, I can tell you whether I'd spend $0, buy a tracking tool, or hire someone—and what I'd expect them to actually do.
